status: 14 original species briefs; proposed ecology, not a runtime food-web implementation
range_units: temperature: normalized -1 cold to +1 hot; moisture: 0 dry to 1 saturated; values are provisional game balancing

species.name: Lantern pod
species.utility: Nursery exports and starter biomass for compatible habitats.
species.tradeoff: Heavy seed harvesting reduces propagation and grazer food.

interactions.effect: Successful visits improve seed set within nutrient and water limits.
Moderate grazing spreads viable seeds; excessive grazing removes biomass.

art.body_plan: Three arching stems with ribbed mint bladders and folded plum leaves.

species.name: Bell grazer
species.utility: Disperses compatible seeds; naturally shed fibers could support insulation production.
species.tradeoff: An abundant herd consumes more crop than its dispersal benefit replaces.

interactions.effect: Moves seed between connected suitable patches.
Predation limits herd growth and can reduce overgrazing.

art.status: candidate GLB and procedural animation exist
art.body_plan: Peach buoyant bell, three independent eyes, side fins and six trailing tendrils.

species.name: Veil reed
species.utility: Traps suspended sediment; membranes enable water-treatment components.
species.tradeoff: Dense stands use shore habitat and slow water exchange; pollution is stored, not magically destroyed.

interactions.effect: Root curtains support detritivore habitat.
Shade reduces local light available to surface colonies.

art.body_plan: Forked stalks carry translucent hanging combs; seed cups resemble listening ears.

species.name: Ember lichen
species.utility: A producer for dim thermal habitats; catalysts can support ore processing.
species.tradeoff: Harvest competes with ecological growth; exhausted vent chemistry cannot support unlimited output.

interactions.effect: A compatible grazer converts some colony biomass into consumer biomass.
Both occupy sheltered mineral pores when their climate tolerances overlap.

art.body_plan: Low ceramic crusts with orange breathing seams and tiny hinged plates.

species.name: Sail frond
species.utility: Collects available fog moisture into sheltered soil; fibers support condensers.
species.tradeoff: No fog means no new water. Water exported from the patch is unavailable to dependent life.

interactions.effect: Retained moisture can permit pods where climate otherwise almost supports them.
Folded sails provide roosts if food and temperature also permit survival.

art.body_plan: Three asymmetrical ribbed sails fold around a fat hooked stem, with hanging droplet sacs.

species.name: Bloom float
species.utility: Supports filter feeders and produces compounds useful in lightweight biological materials.
species.tradeoff: Dense blooms compete for light; dead blooms add a large decomposition load.

interactions.effect: Filter feeding removes bloom biomass.
Surface mats can suppress young reeds through shading.

art.body_plan: Pea-sized luminous beads aggregate into ribbon clouds; render as capped instanced clusters.

species.name: Frostlace
species.utility: Supports cold-world biological products and insulated pockets of habitat.
species.tradeoff: Warming that helps other crops can remove its viable climate niche and a valuable export.

interactions.effect: Cold-tolerant grazer populations can feed on it in overlapping conditions.
Lace mats trap organic litter in sheltered ground.

art.body_plan: Low blue-white fans unfold from dark knots; translucent edges and rose-colored root mouths.

species.name: Pollen imp
species.utility: Improves compatible plant reproduction rather than adding a planet-wide yield bonus.
species.tradeoff: Needs flowers and roosts; predators or habitat loss can remove the service.

interactions.effect: Transfers compatible pollen between surviving flowers.
Too many mantises can suppress the pollinator population.

art.body_plan: Pear-shaped striped abdomen, four leaf wings, one oversized nose and two shy retractable eyes.

species.name: Pebbleback
species.utility: Disturbs compacted substrate and exposes new growth sites.
species.tradeoff: Heavy grazing strips protective ground cover; shell collection depends on natural shedding.

interactions.effect: Moderate scraping opens substrate; high pressure removes the colony.
Egg and juvenile predation limits recruitment.

art.body_plan: Six-footed low stone oval, telescoping snout, mismatched mineral shell plates, soft underside.

species.name: Silt whisk
species.utility: Processes settled organic material and creates habitat for further decomposition.
species.tradeoff: Its activity has a local water-quality cost when organic loading exceeds available capacity.

interactions.effect: Uses protected root curtains; reed removal lowers local carrying capacity.
Processed detritus becomes accessible to sheltered decomposer colonies where conditions overlap.

art.body_plan: Flat transparent tadpole with an enormous brush moustache and paired paddle feet.

species.name: Hush fungus
species.utility: Returns part of consumed dead biomass to available nutrients.
species.tradeoff: No litter means no recovery; excessive decomposition can stress poorly ventilated wet habitat.

interactions.effect: Recycled nutrients can relieve an actual soil shortage.
Uses litter trapped beneath cold-tolerant mats.

art.body_plan: Velvet ear-shaped fruiting bodies above a thin branching mat; pores open in gentle waves.

species.name: Ribbon kite
species.utility: Can reduce a herd's pressure on seed-bearing vegetation.
species.tradeoff: Requires prey; overstocking kills grazers and then starves the predator population.

interactions.effect: Consumes prey biomass; indirectly changes pod grazing pressure.

art.body_plan: Broad petal wings with two long steering ribbons; tiny round face conceals a folding feeding basket.

species.name: Glass mantis
species.utility: Can suppress damaging grazer recruitment around cultivation.
species.tradeoff: Also eats valuable pollinators; introducing it is not automatically beneficial.

interactions.effect: Pollinator loss may reduce seed output.
Egg and juvenile consumption reduces future grazing pressure.

art.body_plan: Four arched legs, transparent spoon arms, leaf-shaped head and a startlingly small smiling mouth.

species.name: Cloud manta
species.utility: A later domestication partnership could support a bounded biological transport route.
species.tradeoff: Needs feeding grounds, rest and suitable air corridors; cargo service competes with recovery time.

interactions.effect: Harvests bloom biomass; excessive suppression harms its own food supply.

art.body_plan: Massive soft kite with a scalloped filter mouth, underslung eye cluster and load-bearing saddle ridges.
